definition: `Actual z`: z is an actual thing. z merely exists when `Actual z ∧ ¬ Lives z` (SCG I.28 [1]: things that merely are, contrasted with living things). Example: a stone. This does not decide whether merely existing things are substances or aggregates.
note: Analyst vocabulary, attribution deferred. AQUINAS-SCG-I28-MERELY-EXISTING-PARTICIPATION keeps the restricted subject 'things that merely exist'; this definition types that subject, not the claim's participation thesis.
